Using Doppler's effect formula:
1) Approaching Train:
$\begin{aligned}
& f_{\text{approach }}=f_0 \times \frac{v}{v-v_0} \\
& F_{\text{recede }}=f_0 \times \frac{v}{v+v_0} \\

& =f_0\left(\frac{v}{v-v_0}-\frac{v}{v+v_0}\right) \\
\Rightarrow \Delta f & =f_0\left(\frac{\left(v+v_0\right)-\left(v-v_0\right)}{\left(v+v_0\right)\left(v-v_0\right)}\right) \\
\Rightarrow \Delta f & =f_0\left(\frac{2 v_0}{v^2-v_s{ }^2}\right) \cdot v \\
v & =330 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s} \\
v_s & =108 \mathrm{ km} / \mathrm{hr}=\frac{108}{1} \times \frac{5}{18}=30 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s} \\
\Rightarrow \Delta f & =f_0 .330 . \frac{2 \times 30}{330^2-30^2} \\
\Delta f & =f_0 \times 330 \times \frac{60}{108000}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \Delta f & =f_0 \cdot \frac{19800}{108000}=f_0 \cdot \frac{11}{60} \\
\% \text{ Change } & =\frac{\Delta f}{f_0} \times 100 \\
& =\frac{11}{60} \times 100=18.33 \%
\end{aligned}\therefore$ ANS: $(A) \%$ Change $=18.33 \%$

questions.q:
A diatomic gas of volume $2m^{3}$ at pressure $2 \times {10}^{5}Nm^{- 2}$ is compressed adiabatically to a volume $0. 5m^{3}.$ The work done in this process is,
[Use ${4}^{1. 4} = 6. 96$]
questions.solution:
In the adiabatic process, the formula of work done in terms of pressure and volume is, $W = \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1} - {P}_{2}{V}_{2}}{\gamma - 1}$

For diatomic gas the value of $\gamma = 1. 4$

Here ${P}_{1} = 2 \times {10}^{5}Nm^{- 2}$, ${V}_{1} = 2m^{3}$ and ${V}_{2} = 0. 5m^{3}$

Put these values in the above formula,
$W = \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1} - {P}_{2}{V}_{2}}{\gamma - 1}$

Here ${P}_{2}\left({V}_{2}\right)\gamma = {P}_{1}\left({V}_{1}\right)\gamma ⇒ {P}_{2} = \dfrac{{P}_{1}\left({V}_{1}\right)\gamma}{\left({V}_{2}\right)\gamma}$
$⇒ W = \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1} - \left(\dfrac{{P}_{1}\left({V}_{1}\right)\gamma}{\left({V}_{2}\right)\gamma}\right){V}_{2}}{\gamma - 1} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{5} \times 2 - \left(\dfrac{2 \times {10}^{5}\left(2\right)^{1}. 4}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{1}. 4}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}}{1. 4 - 1} ⇒ W = - 7. 4 \times {10}^{5}J$

Phase of given wave is

Differentiating with respect to time,

questions.q: If the length of a stretched string is shortened by $40 \%$ and the tension is increased by $44 \%$, then the ratio of the final and initial fundamental frequencies is :

Fundamental frequency, $n=\frac{1}{2 l} \sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}$
Initial frequency, $n_1=\frac{1}{2 l} \sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}$
New length, $l^{\prime}=l-\frac{l \times 40}{100}=0.6 l$
New tension, $T^{\prime}=T+\frac{T \times 44}{100}=1.44 \mathrm{ T}$
New frequency $n_2=\frac{1}{2 l^{\prime}} \sqrt{\frac{T^{\prime}}{m}}\therefore \quad \frac{n_2}{n_1}=\frac{\frac{1}{2 l^{\prime}} \sqrt{\frac{T^{\prime}}{m}}}{\frac{1}{2 l} \sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}}\frac{n_2}{n_1}=\frac{l}{l^{\prime}} \sqrt{\left(\frac{T^{\prime}}{T}\right)}=\frac{l}{0.6 l} \sqrt{\frac{1.44 T}{T}}=\frac{1}{0.6} \times 1.2=2\therefore \quad n_2: n_1=2: 1$
